site.name: World Zombie Day: London
site.description: World Zombie Day: London is a free, family-friendly Community Fundraising event: a zombie walk through central London. Saturday 10 October 2026.
home.hero.title: World Zombie Day: London
home.hero.standfirst: The zombies couldn’t stay buried forever. After a hiatus since 2019, the London branch has been resurrected, and we’re shambling back with more excitement than ever before.
home.essentials.title: The essentials
home.essentials.when.label: When
home.essentials.when.value: Saturday 10 October 2026. World Zombie Day always falls on the second Saturday of October.
home.essentials.where.label: Where
home.essentials.where.value: Central London. The meeting point is confidential and goes out to everyone who registers a few days before the event.
home.essentials.cost.label: Cost
home.essentials.cost.value: Free. There’s an optional “pay what you can” donation. £5 is the suggested amount, and everything beyond running costs goes to the cause we’re fundraising for.
home.essentials.who.label: Who it’s for
home.essentials.who.value: Everyone. Family-friendly, dog-friendly, and planned with step-free routes for prams and wheelchairs. Under-18s need a parent or guardian with them.
home.essentials.wear.label: What to wear
home.essentials.wear.value: Your best zombie attire is highly recommended but not required. No weapons of any kind, real or fake.
home.about.title: What is World Zombie Day?
home.about.body1: World Zombie Day was born in Pittsburgh’s Monroeville Mall in 2006, the location of George Romero’s Dawn of the Dead. More than 50 cities worldwide now take part, including New York, Pittsburgh, Paris, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas, Seattle and Tokyo.
home.about.body2: The idea is simple: fans of zombie culture come together, take over a bit of the city for an afternoon, and raise money for a good cause while doing it. London has been shambling since 2011.
home.day.title: What happens on the day
home.day.body1: Hundreds of zombies meet at a confidential starting point in central London, check in with a steward, and shamble a route between locations across the afternoon, groaning, posing for photographs, and collecting donations along the way.
home.day.body2: Stewards in high-vis lead the walk and keep everyone safe at crossings. There are scheduled pauses for photos, so there’s no need to hold up the horde for a shot.
home.cause.title: Who we’re raising money for
home.cause.body1: This year the horde is fundraising for The Dead Good Club, a Community Interest Company that exists to help people reclaim their attention, build AI and digital media literacy, and stay human in a fast-changing technological world.
home.cause.body2: The club fights brain rot without blaming people for being overwhelmed, teaches AI and media literacy so people can understand the systems shaping their attention, and creates phone-free spaces where people can make things and meet each other.
home.cause.body3: It celebrates horror, neurospicy, outsider creativity and community through events, awards, zines, tools and workshops. The approach is not anti-AI. It is pro-human: using technology knowingly, refusing it deliberately, and protecting creativity, privacy, attention and dignity.
home.cta.title: Join the horde
home.cta.body: Registration is essential. It’s how we send you the meeting point, the route and everything else you need to know.
register.title: Register
register.standfirst: Experience the thrill of London’s reanimated zombie walk through the heart of the city. Don your most impressive zombie attire and join fellow enthusiasts for an unforgettable journey through iconic London locations. A gory-good celebration of horror, creativity, and community.
register.status.title: Register for 2026
register.why.title: Why you have to register
register.why.body: Registration is essential to receive confidential meeting point information.
register.cost.title: What it costs
register.cost.body: This event remains free to attend. If you can, we invite you to make an optional pay-what-you-can donation (£5 is recommended). Every contribution supports The Dead Good Club, helping us fund community projects, education, events, and keeping World Zombie Day possible.
register.access.title: Accessible to all, family-friendly and dog-friendly
register.access.body:
Bring the whole horde out for the day! Children with spooky dispositions will enjoy this perfect primer to Halloween events. All participants under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

Well-behaved dogs on leads are welcome to join their undead owners. Accessible routes are planned for pushchairs and wheelchairs.
register.cause.title: Supporting a worthy cause
register.cause.body: World Zombie Day is made possible by the support of The Dead Good Club, which exists to help people reclaim their attention, build AI and digital media literacy, and stay human in a fast-changing technological world.
register.involved.title: Get involved
register.involved.body: Help out by volunteering your time, assisting with fundraising, or simply spreading the word. Get in touch to join the event team.
rules.title: Zombie rules of conduct
rules.standfirst: Put on a good show. Stay in character but don’t get carried away. You are responsible for your own safety and good conduct.
rules.1: Use the “haunted house” rule: you are not to touch anyone.
rules.2: Use your best judgement when planning your outfit. Do not bring weapons of any kind: fake, fantasy, or definitely not real. You’ll be on your feet and outdoors for most of the day, so take that into consideration. And be creative!
rules.3: Do not attempt to scare anyone who is not a willing participant. If anyone is freaking out, turn and shamble in the opposite direction. Avoid confrontations.
rules.4: Where the walk is near streets or roadways, stay on the pavement unless crossing. When crossing, it’s fine to break character and cross quickly. Think fast “New Dawn of the Dead” zombies rather than the slower “Old Dawn of the Dead” ones. Blocking traffic is a crime and anyone doing so could be arrested.
rules.5: Strictly no illegal drugs, and no alcohol for under-18s. Police will be called if this rule is broken.
rules.6: No littering, destruction of property, or any other illegal activity. That includes smearing fake blood and banging on windows.
rules.7: You might be asked for photo ID at the pubs, and your zombie face might not match it. If you are refused entry, please understand the doorman is only doing his job.
rules.8: Do not attempt to push your way into any business if you are not welcome.
rules.stewards.title: Stewards are there to help
rules.stewards.body: Stewards in high-vis lead the walk, manage crossings and answer questions. If you see any behaviour that concerns you, speak to a steward.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.standfirst: Some commonly asked questions and their answers.
faq.a1: Saturday 10 October 2026. World Zombie Day always occurs on the second Saturday of October.
faq.q2: Where will the event take place? How do I get there?
faq.a2: The event details are revealed a few days before the event to everyone who has registered. The locations are typically in central London and easy to reach on the Underground. If you need special arrangements, email info@worldzombieday.co.uk.
faq.a3: Yes! Bring the whole horde out for the day. Children with spooky dispositions will enjoy this perfect primer to Halloween events. All participants under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
faq.a4: Yes, this is a dog-friendly event. Well-behaved dogs on leads are welcome to join their undead owners.
faq.q5: Will there be stairs or accessibility restrictions?
faq.a5: Every effort is made to choose locations that are accessible, but as we head to several locations on the day there may be obstructions or road blocks that require alternative routes.
faq.q6: Is there a specific dress code?
faq.a6: Your best zombie attire is highly recommended, but not required. Please be mindful that this is a public event. You will be seen by locals and tourists of all ages, and are likely to be photographed or filmed.
faq.a7: No. Please do not bring protest signs or use this event for any political agenda or demonstration.
faq.a8: Nothing. The event is free, with an optional “pay what you can” donation, £5 suggested. Everything beyond running costs goes to the cause we’re fundraising for.
faq.more.title: Still stuck?
faq.more.body: Email info@worldzombieday.co.uk and we’ll get back to you.
sponsors.title: Become a sponsor
sponsors.standfirst: We are always open to new sponsors, with the primary aim of raising funds for the cause.
sponsors.intro1: Our sponsors help us by contributing directly to the cause we’re fundraising for, or by helping with our admin costs.
sponsors.intro2: Each year hundreds of enthusiastic zombies take part, and we are typically featured in major publications including Time Out, BuzzFeed, The Guardian and The Huffington Post.
sponsors.options.title: Sponsorship options
sponsors.onsite.title: On-site promotion
sponsors.onsite.body1: As we move from location to location throughout the day, on-site promotion should either be mobile or limited to one stop.
sponsors.onsite.body2: Be creative. We ask that you run any concepts by us so we can make sure they’re aligned with the event and the cause. Beyond that you have free rein.
sponsors.onsite.examples.title: Things sponsors have done before
sponsors.onsite.example2: “Breaking news: zombie outbreak reported in central London”
sponsors.onsite.example3: Phone apps reviewed by real zombies
sponsors.onsite.noflyering.title: No flyering
sponsors.onsite.noflyering.body: It’s important to us that nobody hands out flyers or anything else likely to become litter. Stickers or stamps are good alternatives.
sponsors.prize.title: Online prize giveaway
sponsors.prize.body: We typically get 1,500 people registering for World Zombie Day: London. A description of your prize and information about your organisation is shown to everyone who registers.
sponsors.prize.item1: Send us a summary of the prize, its value, and an image or video to advertise it.
sponsors.prize.item2: Include a redemption or promo code, or tell us how the winner will receive the prize. If you have specific terms you use for raffles let us know, otherwise we’ll use a generic set.
sponsors.contact.title: Get in touch
sponsors.contact.body: If you are interested in becoming a sponsor, email info@worldzombieday.co.uk.
photo.title: Photo policy
photo.standfirst: We love seeing all the wonderful images of you bloody creative zombies after the big day.
photo.intro1: We are ever grateful to everyone who has documented and shared their highlights from World Zombie Day: London. Keep them coming this year.
photo.intro2: All are welcome to photograph or film on the day. Here are some things you should know about our photo and video policy.
photo.basics.1: Filming and photography happen throughout the day, by freelance and vocational photographers, by press, and by our sponsors.
photo.basics.2: If you are attending only to photograph or film, you still need to register to receive the starting location, route and other relevant information.
photo.basics.3: You are not obliged to attend as a zombie, but it is encouraged.
photo.credit.title: Please include this text when you post
photo.credit.body: The purpose of World Zombie Day is to raise money for good causes. Join the zombies in fundraising for The Dead Good Club, committed to fighting brain rot. A pro-human Community Interest Company helping people build healthier digital habits in a post-human era. To donate go to: paa.ge/worldzombieday
photo.credit.tags: And please tag anything you post with #WZD2026 and #WorldZombieDay.
photo.rules.title: Rules of engagement
photo.rule1.title: 1. Safety and consent
photo.rule1.item1: Respect a zombie’s wishes if they do not want to be photographed or filmed.
photo.rule1.item2: Do not intentionally obstruct anyone’s path, shop entrances, streets or traffic.
photo.rule1.important: Important: do not hold up the walk for photo shoots or take participants aside. We have agreed timings with the city and disruption has knock-on effects. There are times set aside in the day where we pause for photos, so please help us stick to the schedule.
photo.rule2.title: 2. No unauthorised commercial sales
photo.rule2.item1: Photographers may not sell photos directly to event participants.
photo.rule2.item2: Distributing “spec”, proof or access cards for personal financial gain is strictly prohibited.
photo.rule2.item3: Soliciting money, tips or digital payments from guests for photos is banned.
photo.rule3.title: 3. Focus on the cause
photo.rule3.item1: All photographs taken at this event must support the cause we’re fundraising for.
photo.rule3.item2: Images should be used to promote the cause, thank donors, or share the event’s success.
photo.consent.title: Consent
photo.consent.body: All those who participate in this event may be filmed and/or photographed, and give consent for any filmed footage or other likeness, picture, photograph, portrait or moving image (in whole or in part) to be used and/or published or broadcast for marketing, social media and public relations purposes without further limitation and in perpetuity.
photo.press.title: Press
photo.press.body: Members of the press: please contact info@worldzombieday.co.uk with any enquiries, or head to the press kit for logos, photography and boilerplate.
photo.credits.title: The photographers
photo.credits.body: Every photograph on this site was taken by someone who gave their time to the event. Please credit them if you share their work.
press.title: Press kit
press.standfirst: Everything you need to cover World Zombie Day: London: boilerplate, key facts, logos and photography.
press.contact.title: Press contact
press.boiler.short.title: Short boilerplate
press.boiler.short.body: World Zombie Day: London is a free Community Fundraising event, a zombie walk through central London, held on the second Saturday of October. In 2026 it returns on Saturday 10 October, raising money for The Dead Good Club, a Community Interest Company.
press.boiler.long.title: Long boilerplate
press.boiler.long.body: World Zombie Day is an international annual event that grew from Pittsburgh’s first zombie walk at Monroeville Mall in 2006, the site where George Romero filmed Dawn of the Dead. Its aim is to bring fans of zombie culture together in an international effort to raise money for good causes, and more than 50 cities now take part. The London walk has been running since 2011 and typically draws around 1,500 registrations; it returns on Saturday 10 October 2026 after a hiatus, raising money for The Dead Good Club, a Community Interest Company. The event is free, family-friendly and dog-friendly, and open to anyone who wants to shamble.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.standfirst: What World Zombie Day: London collects, why, and what you can ask us to do about it.
privacy.who.title: Who we are
privacy.who.body: World Zombie Day: London is a free, volunteer-run Community Fundraising event. For data protection purposes we are the data controller for this website and for event registrations. You can reach us at info@worldzombieday.co.uk.
privacy.collect.title: What we collect
privacy.collect.reg.title: When you register for the walk
privacy.collect.reg.body: Your email address, and whatever else the registration form asks for that year. We use it to send you the meeting point, the route, and safety updates, nothing else.
privacy.collect.contact.title: When you email us
privacy.collect.contact.body: Your email address and whatever you write to us, kept as long as we need it to answer you.
privacy.collect.analytics.title: When you browse this site
privacy.collect.analytics.body: If you accept, we use PostHog and Google Analytics 4 to count visits and see which pages people read, so we know what to improve. They record the pages you view, where you arrived from, roughly where in the world you are, and what kind of device and browser you use. We do not use them to identify you, session recording is off, autocapture is off, your IP address is anonymised, and we do not track you across other websites. If you decline, neither of them is ever loaded.
privacy.why.title: Why we are allowed to
privacy.why.body: For registration emails, because you asked us to send them. That is your consent, and you can withdraw it at any time. For analytics and for answering your messages, our legitimate interest in running a safe event and a website that works. We never rely on legitimate interests where your rights clearly outweigh ours.
privacy.cookies.title: Cookies and your choice
privacy.cookies.body: Nothing is stored on your device unless you accept it. The bar at the foot of the page asks once, covering all three things that would store anything: PostHog and Google Analytics, which tell us which pages are read, and the registration form, which is run by Zeffy and needs its own cookies to take a booking or a payment. Decline and none of them load at all; the rest of the site works exactly the same, and you can still register by opening the form on Zeffy's own site. Two things are kept whatever you choose, because they are the choices themselves: your answer to this question, and your theme, dark or light.
privacy.sharing.title: Who else sees it
privacy.sharing.body: PostHog and Google process analytics data on our behalf, and Vercel hosts the site and keeps standard server logs. All three are bound to act only on our instructions. Registrations and donations are handled by Zeffy, who are the controller for whatever you enter into their form. We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with anyone else unless the law requires it.
privacy.retention.title: How long we keep it
privacy.retention.body: Registration details are deleted within twelve months of the event they were for. Analytics data is kept for up to twelve months. Emails are deleted once the conversation is finished and there is no reason to keep it.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.body: Under UK data protection law you can ask us for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, or object to us using it. Email info@worldzombieday.co.uk and we will respond within one month.
privacy.rights.complain: If you think we have got it wrong, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk. We would rather you told us first so we can put it right.
privacy.photos.title: Photography
privacy.photos.body: This is a public event and participants may be photographed or filmed. The photo policy covers what that means, how images are used, and how to ask not to be photographed.
privacy.changes.title: Changes
privacy.changes.body: If this policy changes we will update the date at the top of this page. Material changes will be flagged on the registration page before the next event.
register.cause.donation: Your donation helps keep World Zombie Day safe, accessible, and free to attend, while supporting The Dead Good Club’s year-round community work:
register.cause.work.1: Stop the Rot: Fight brain rot without blaming people for being overwhelmed.
register.cause.work.2: Reclaim Your Brain: Teach AI and media literacy so people can understand the systems shaping their attention, choices, and culture.
register.cause.work.3: Mobile Free Mondays: Create phone-free, real-world spaces and opportunities where people can make things, meet others, and reconnect with their own minds.
register.cause.work.4: Celebrate horror, neurospicy, outsider creativity, and community through events, awards, zines, tools, and workshops.
register.cause.work.5: Stay pro-human: Not anti-AI, but focused on using technology knowingly, refusing it deliberately, and protecting creativity, privacy, attention, and dignity.
register.cause.thanks: Every registration for this event brings us closer to achieving that mission. Thank you for supporting our mission. Your support is invaluable.
donate.title: Donate
donate.standfirst: The walk is free to join. Everything beyond the cost of running it safely goes to The Dead Good Club, and you can give whatever you can, whether or not you are coming on the day.
donate.how.title: Where the money goes
donate.other.title: Other ways to help
donate.other.body: Sponsor the event, offer a prize, or lend us a skill for the day. Sponsorship keeps the walk free to attend, which is the thing we protect above everything else.
